content: Cefepime is a cephalosporin antibiotic used to treat a variety of bacterial infections. It is administered either intravenously (IV) or intramuscularly (IM) based on the condition being treated. The dosage and duration of treatment depend on the severity of the infection and the patient’s medical condition. For severe urinary tract infections (UTIs) caused by Escherichia coli or Klebsiella pneumoniae, the recommended dose is 2 grams IV every 12 hours for 10 days. For uncomplicated skin and skin structure infections, the dose is also 2 grams IV every 12 hours for 10 days. In cases of complicated intra-abdominal infections, cefepime should be used in combination with metronidazole at a dose of 2 grams IV every 12 hours for 7–10 days. Dosage adjustments are necessary for patients with impaired kidney function, based on creatinine clearance (CrCl). In febrile neutropenic patients over 2 months of age and weighing less than 40 kg, the recommended dose is 50 mg/kg IV every 8 hours for 7 days or until neutropenia resolves, with a maximum dose of 2 grams every 8 hours. For moderate-to-severe pneumonia, the dose is 50 mg/kg IV every 12 hours for 10 days, not exceeding 2 grams every 12 hours. For uncomplicated and complicated UTIs, including pyelonephritis, the dose is 50 mg/kg IV or IM every 12 hours for 7–10 days, with a maximum of 2 grams every 12 hours. Cefepime interacts with several medications and vaccines. It can reduce the efficacy of live bacterial vaccines, such as the BCG vaccine, typhoid vaccine, and cholera vaccine, due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. It is recommended to avoid co-administration of these vaccines with cefepime and wait until antibiotic treatment is completed before administering live bacterial vaccines. Additionally, cefepime may decrease the effectiveness of oral microbiota products and hormonal contraceptives by altering intestinal flora. Patients using oral contraceptives should consider alternative or additional forms of birth control during cefepime therapy. Cefepime may increase the nephrotoxic and ototoxic effects of aminoglycosides, such as amikacin, gentamicin, kanamycin, neomycin, plazomicin, streptomycin, and tobramycin. Caution and close monitoring of renal function are advised when these drugs are co-administered. Similarly, co-administration with potent diuretics like furosemide may increase the risk of nephrotoxicity, and renal function should be monitored. Cefepime may also interfere with the therapeutic effects of immune checkpoint inhibitors, such as atezolizumab, avelumab, balstilimab, camrelizumab, cemiplimab, dostarlimab, durvalumab, nivolumab, pembrolizumab, penpulimab, retifanlimab, sintilimab, tislelizumab, and toripalimab. Caution and monitoring are recommended when these agents are used concurrently. Probenecid can increase cefepime levels by competing for renal tubular clearance, necessitating caution and monitoring. Cefepime may also increase the effects of warfarin by reducing prothrombin activity, requiring careful monitoring of coagulation parameters. Cefepime is minimally metabolized in the liver, with most of the drug (85%) excreted unchanged in the urine. It has a half-life of approximately 2 hours and a volume of distribution (Vd) of 16–20 liters in adults. It penetrates inflammatory fluids at concentrations around 80% of serum levels and crosses the blood-brain barrier. Common side effects include swelling, redness, or pain at the injection site. Rarely, cefepime may cause a severe intestinal condition due to Clostridioides difficile infection, which can occur during or after treatment. Prolonged or repeated use may lead to oral thrush or yeast infections. Serious allergic reactions are rare but possible. Cefepime passes into breast milk in small amounts and is unlikely to harm a nursing infant. However, the benefits of breastfeeding should be weighed against the mother’s clinical need for cefepime and any potential adverse effects on the infant. Patients should complete the full course of cefepime as prescribed, even if symptoms improve, to prevent the development of antibiotic resistance. If a dose is missed, patients should consult their healthcare provider for guidance. Proper storage and disposal of the medication are essential, and patients should follow the instructions provided by their pharmacist. This information is not exhaustive and does not replace professional medical advice. Patients should consult their healthcare provider for personalized guidance regarding cefepime use and potential interactions.
